title: Computationally guided high-throughput design of self-assembling drug nanoparticles.
summary: Machine learning integrated with high-throughput experiments identified 100 self-assembling drug nanoparticles from 2.1 million drug/excipient pairings. Two formulations were further characterized ex vivo and in vivo; the reviewed abstract does not establish clinical benefit.
organization: Brigham and Women's Hospital; Harvard University; Duke University

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports 100 self-assembling formulations identified from a search space of 2.1 million drug/excipient pairings (788 drugs, 2,686 excipients). Sorafenib–glycyrrhizin and terbinafine–taurocholic acid received further ex-vivo/in-vivo characterization. Actual physical-screen denominator, sample sizes and controls were not assessed.
evidence.unknown: Only publisher abstract and metadata were reviewed; article Methods and supplement were inaccessible through PMC due CAPTCHA. Model architecture, screen controls, sample sizes and detailed ex-vivo/in-vivo outcomes were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: The abstract confirms machine learning integrated with high-throughput experimentation; model architecture and precise selection operation were not assessable from the reviewed material.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary PubMed metadata and author-institution abstract; complete Nature/PMC Methods and supplement not accessible.
